name: Pharmacogenomics Clinical Interpretation Readiness
purpose: Explain when the curated PGx marker components are incomplete and identify the clinical inputs required before a drug-specific phenotype or prescribing decision can be considered.

policy.summary: The report may show individual PGx marker components, but a consumer DNA array is not a complete clinical result. CPIC's antidepressant guidance depends on the medicine: CYP2C19 for citalopram, escitalopram, and sertraline; CYP2B6 also for sertraline; and CYP2D6 for paroxetine, fluvoxamine, venlafaxine, and vortioxetine. Advice varies by medicine and complete clinical result. CPIC gives no gene-based fluoxetine dosing advice, and SLC6A4 or HTR2A results are not supported for antidepressant prescribing. A complete clinical result may help explain medicine levels and general side-effect risk; DNA is not validated to predict emotional numbness. This report does not check combinations of medicines.
policy.display_rule: Describe which DNA components are present and what is missing; never assign a metabolizer type, dose, medicine choice, toxicity diagnosis, or treatment change from a single raw-DNA marker. Do not present DNA as predicting emotional numbness. This report is not a medicine-interaction checker; for fluoxetine, CPIC gives no gene-based dosing advice, and SLC6A4 or HTR2A results are not supported for antidepressant prescribing.
required_inputs: Exact drug name, indication, formulation, and current dose when relevant
Complete clinical PGx result or validated laboratory assay method
Star-allele diplotype, phase, or phenotype when the gene requires it
Copy-number, structural-variant, repeat, or HLA typing where relevant
Current medications, interactions, organ function, symptoms, and clinician or pharmacist interpretation
do_not_claim: A complete PGx phenotype from one or a few consumer-array SNPs
A medication dose, medication choice, or treatment change from raw DNA
A negative consumer-array result as exclusion of a rare allele, CNV, HLA allele, or enzyme deficiency
Medication toxicity, treatment failure, or symptom causation from a genotype alone

genes.label: CYP2D6 result and antidepressant context
genes.limitation: CYP2D6 phenotype requires both star alleles plus copy-number, hybrid, and additional-variant assessment; consumer arrays may not capture structural variation or phase. CPIC has drug-specific CYP2D6 guidance for some medicines, including paroxetine and fluvoxamine; for fluoxetine, it finds the overall active drug level and clinical impact unclear and gives no gene-based dosing recommendation. No clinically validated DNA prediction of emotional numbness is established here.
required_inputs: Prior medicine-specific response or side effects, dose, timing, and interaction review
genes.clinical_next_step: If fluoxetine caused emotional numbness or another unwanted effect, share the medicine, dose, timing, and what happened with the prescriber. CYP2D6 consumer markers cannot confirm the cause or predict the same effect, and CPIC gives no gene-based fluoxetine dosing recommendation.

genes.label: CYP2C19 result and SSRI context
genes.limitation: The listed SNPs are pieces of a result, not a full CYP2C19 clinical type. For sertraline, some complete CYP2C19 results can mean higher medicine levels and may help a clinician consider general side-effect risk; they do not predict emotional numbness. One small 8-week study in adolescents found no link between CYP2C19 and emotional-blunting scores; it does not settle effects in adults.
required_inputs: Prior medicine-specific response or side effects, dose, and timing
Interactions and prescriber or pharmacist context
genes.clinical_next_step: If sertraline caused emotional numbness, tell the prescriber what you took, the dose, when it began, and how it changed. Ask whether clinical PGx interpretation could help explain how your body processes sertraline; current evidence cannot reliably predict that specific effect from DNA.

genes.label: CYP2B6 result and sertraline context
genes.limitation: rs3745274 is one of the two core variants used to define CYP2B6*6; rs2279343 is the other. This marker alone cannot establish the haplotype or a clinical phenotype. CPIC's CYP2B6 sertraline recommendations for intermediate or poor phenotypes are optional and based mainly on pharmacokinetic evidence; they are not validated to predict emotional numbness. CYP2C19 results, interactions, and clinical context also matter.
required_inputs: Validated CYP2B6 genotype or phenotype with adequate allele coverage
CYP2C19 result and interaction review when sertraline is relevant
Prior medicine-specific response or side effects and clinician or pharmacist interpretation
genes.clinical_next_step: If sertraline caused emotional numbness, share that history and its dose and timing with the prescriber. This single CYP2B6 marker cannot establish the clinical phenotype or predict the effect; do not change treatment from raw DNA.

genes.label: CYP2C9 diplotype and drug-specific interpretation
genes.limitation: Reduced-function components can contribute to a clinical CYP2C9 diplotype, but the other allele, rare variants, drug, indication, and co-factors determine interpretation.
required_inputs: Kidney, liver, bleeding-risk, and interaction context when relevant
genes.clinical_next_step: For NSAIDs, warfarin, phenytoin, or another drug-specific question, bring the complete result to the prescriber or pharmacist; do not self-select or dose medication from a component marker.

genes.label: SLCO1B1 transporter haplotype and statin context
genes.limitation: These markers are transporter or haplotype components. A drug-specific clinical interpretation also depends on the complete allele definition, statin, dose, interactions, symptoms, and medical context.
required_inputs: Drug interactions and thyroid or organ-function context
genes.clinical_next_step: Use the result as a prompt for pharmacist or prescriber review if statin therapy is relevant; it does not diagnose myopathy or require a medication change.

genes.label: Warfarin multi-gene context
genes.limitation: Warfarin dosing is a multi-factor clinical algorithm using VKORC1, CYP2C9, CYP4F2, age, weight, interacting medicines, diet, indication, and measured INR; these two markers are not a dose calculator.
genes.clinical_next_step: If warfarin is being used or considered, discuss the complete clinical context with the anticoagulation team; never adjust warfarin from the consumer report.

genes.label: DPYD fluoropyrimidine safety interpretation
genes.limitation: The listed variants are selected DPYD components and do not establish normal enzyme activity or exclude other decreased-function alleles. Treatment decisions require an oncology-led clinical result and regimen context.
required_inputs: Validated DPYD result or phenotype assessment
Clinical history, organ function, and monitoring plan
genes.clinical_next_step: Any DPYD finding should be brought to the oncology team before fluoropyrimidine treatment decisions; do not interpret a missing call as normal activity.

genes.label: TPMT and NUDT15 thiopurine interpretation
genes.limitation: Thiopurine risk interpretation uses complete TPMT/NUDT15 allele coverage or enzyme/phenotype testing, the drug and indication, and clinical monitoring; a few SNPs are not a complete safety clearance.
required_inputs: Complete TPMT and NUDT15 clinical result or phenotype
Relevant ancestry, interactions, and organ-function context
genes.clinical_next_step: Ask the prescriber or pharmacist whether clinical TPMT/NUDT15 testing and monitoring are needed; never start, stop, or dose a thiopurine from raw DNA alone.

genes.label: UGT1A1 repeat and irinotecan context
genes.limitation: UGT1A1*28 is a promoter repeat and the tag SNP is not the repeat itself; a clinical interpretation requires repeat-aware testing, other alleles, drug/regimen, and patient context.
required_inputs: Repeat-aware or complete UGT1A1 clinical result
Blood-count, liver, and oncology context when relevant
genes.clinical_next_step: Treat the tag or repeat as a prompt for clinical review, not a diagnosis or irinotecan dose instruction.

genes.label: HLA drug-hypersensitivity typing
genes.limitation: Consumer-array SNPs and proxy markers are not equivalent to clinical HLA typing. The exact HLA allele and drug-specific indication must be established by a validated assay before a clinical safety decision.
required_inputs: Urgent care for suspected severe drug reaction
genes.clinical_next_step: Use the finding only to ask whether clinical HLA typing is appropriate; do not label a person safe or unsafe for a drug from a consumer tag.

genes.label: G6PD variant and enzyme-activity context
genes.limitation: Selected G6PD variants do not measure current enzyme activity, capture every clinically relevant allele, or account for transfusion, hemolysis, sex-chromosome context, or treatment circumstances.
required_inputs: Quantitative or validated clinical G6PD testing
Clinician review before a high-risk exposure
genes.clinical_next_step: Ask a clinician about confirmatory enzyme or molecular testing when medication or exposure risk is relevant; do not treat an uncalled marker as proof of normal G6PD activity.

genes.label: CYP3A5 tacrolimus interpretation
genes.limitation: CYP3A5*3 is one component of a clinical interpretation. Tacrolimus management requires transplant indication, complete result, interacting medicines, and measured trough levels.
genes.clinical_next_step: Keep any dose decision with the transplant team; a consumer marker is not a tacrolimus dose instruction.

genes.label: NAT2 acetylator-component context
genes.limitation: NAT2 acetylator status is a haplotype or diplotype interpretation, not a single-SNP result, and its clinical relevance depends on the exact drug and indication.
genes.clinical_next_step: Use the components to prompt drug-specific clinical review only; do not call someone a rapid or slow acetylator from one marker.

do_not_do: Do not infer medication response, toxicity, treatment failure, or dose from raw consumer DNA alone.
Do not use a missing array marker to rule out a pharmacogenomic allele or clinical phenotype.
Do not let a PGx component override current symptoms, contraindications, organ function, drug interactions, or prescriber instructions.
Do not treat a clinical guideline as evidence that this raw-DNA report has already produced the required clinical phenotype call.
